lines.text: Ancient kingdoms, a colony, a divided peninsula and a state ruled by one family. This is the story of North Korea.
Tradition says the first Korean kingdom, Gojoseon, was founded by Dangun in 2333 BCE. It fell to China's Han dynasty much later.
In the north rose Goguryeo, a kingdom that held off Chinese invasions and left painted tombs still admired today.
Goryeo united the peninsula and gave Korea its name. Its craftsmen made celadon pottery and printed with metal type.
Then came Joseon, which ruled for five centuries from Seoul, and gave Korea its own alphabet, Hangul.
In 1912 Kim Il Sung was born. He would found North Korea and build a state around himself.
His son Kim Jong Il would take over at his death, and rule for seventeen years.
After Japanese rule ended and the peninsula was divided, North Korea was founded in 1948, a one-party state under Kim.
In 1950 the north invaded the south. America and its allies came to one side, China to the other, and the war ended in an armistice.
That armistice left a strip of land about four kilometres wide across the peninsula, one of the most heavily guarded borders in the world.
Ever since, people have tried to escape, usually through China. Tens of thousands have reached the south.
In the fifties, Kim set out Juche, the idea of self-reliance that became the state's creed.
In 1976, in the Demilitarized Zone, North Korean soldiers killed two American officers in a dispute over a tree.
Kim Jong Un was born, the grandson who would lead the country from 2011.
In Pyongyang, work began on the Ryugyong Hotel, a pyramid-shaped tower that has never opened.
In the nineties, after Kim Il Sung's death, a great famine swept the country.
In 2006, North Korea carried out its first nuclear test.
By 2017 it tested the Hwasong-15, a missile that could reach the whole of the United States.
Then, in 2018, a thaw. The leaders of the two Koreas met and shook hands.
In Singapore, for the first time, a North Korean leader met an American president.
And from 2024, North Korea sent its soldiers to fight for Russia against Ukraine.
Old kingdoms gave way to a closed state, still divided from its neighbours in the south.
